title: Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

reading.body:
This is a case of likeness fabrication used as harassment. A real person's photographs were taken from a private account and run through AI image generation to produce explicit images of her, which were then circulated as if they depicted her. The failure is not a model stating something false in the course of a task. It is a person using a generative tool to manufacture a false depiction of an identifiable individual and distributing it under invented identities.

The generation happened outside any system that could have reviewed it, and the distribution happened across Instagram, Discord and Facebook through multiple fake accounts and email addresses. Nothing in the reporting describes a platform detecting the images or the accounts. The conduct came to light because anonymous accounts messaged the victim to tell her the images were on Discord servers, and she then reported it to the Cyber Police Station in North Delhi. Catching it earlier would have required either linking the fake accounts to a single person before the victim was contacted, or preventing the source photographs from being used this way at all.

What is not established is which AI tool produced the images, and the investigation is continuing, with other unknown users having created additional explicit content that Bansal then shared. The stated motive comes from his own confession rather than from an independent finding.

reports.title: Delhi: Man held for circulating obscene AI-generated photos of college acquaintance
Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

summary:
A 22-year-old man named Keshav Bansal was arrested in Delhi for creating and spreading explicit artificial intelligence-generated images of a college acquaintance without her consent. Bansal, a BTech graduate, obtained photographs from the woman's private social media account and used AI technology to create obscene morphed images. He then distributed this content through multiple fake accounts on Instagram, Discord, and Facebook while using various email addresses to hide his identity.

The victim discovered the harassment when she received messages from anonymous accounts informing her that her altered images were being shared on Discord servers. She reported the matter to the Cyber Police Station in North Delhi. Investigators analyzed digital footprints and traced the fake accounts back to Bansal, who confessed that personal resentment from college had motivated his actions. Police recovered his mobile phone, SIM cards, and digital evidence. The investigation is continuing as authorities noted that other unknown users had also created additional explicit content that Bansal subsequently shared.
